record.paper_title: A Proximal Quasi-Newton Trust-Region Method for Nonsmooth Regularized Optimization
record.original_question: Can the convergence and complexity results for the nonsmooth regularized trust-region framework be extended to more general nonlinear stepsize-control methods?

evidence.quote: more general nonlinear stepsize control-type methods

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the composite nonsmooth optimization problem
    minimize over x in R^n   φ(x) := f(x) + h(x),
where f : R^n → R is continuously differentiable with Lipschitz-continuous gradient (or, more generally, satisfies a standard smoothness/model-accuracy condition) and h : R^n → R ∪ {+∞} is proper and lower semicontinuous, possibly nonconvex and nonsmooth.

A proximal quasi-Newton trust-region algorithm for this problem proceeds as follows. At iterate x_k with trust-region radius Δ_k > 0, one builds a (possibly nonconvex) model
    m_k(s) = f(x_k) + ⟨∇f(x_k), s⟩ + ½ ⟨s, B_k s⟩ + h(x_k + s),
where B_k is a symmetric quasi-Newton approximation, computes an approximate minimizer s_k of m_k(s) subject to ‖s‖ ≤ Δ_k that achieves a sufficient decrease in the model relative to a prox-gradient (Cauchy) step, and accepts or rejects s_k by comparing the actual reduction φ(x_k) − φ(x_k + s_k) to the predicted reduction m_k(0) − m_k(s_k), adapting Δ_k accordingly. Under standard hypotheses this scheme is known to converge to a first-order stationary point and to achieve a worst-case iteration complexity of O(ε^{-2}) for driving a stationarity measure below ε.

A nonlinear stepsize control (NSC) framework in the sense of Toint is a unified scheme that controls the size of the trial step through a scalar parameter via a nonlinear control rule, encompassing trust-region methods, adaptive regularization methods (such as quadratic and cubic regularization), and related step-control strategies as special cases.

Problem. Extend the global convergence theory and the worst-case iteration complexity bound described above for the proximal quasi-Newton trust-region method for nonsmooth regularized problems to a general nonlinear stepsize control framework: formulate a proximal quasi-Newton NSC algorithm for the composite problem min_x f(x) + h(x) with f smooth and h proper lower semicontinuous, prove its global convergence to first-order stationary points, and establish a worst-case complexity bound that recovers, as special cases, the trust-region and adaptive regularization variants.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results show active follow-up work on proximal trust-region and proximal modified quasi-Newton methods for nonsmooth regularized optimization (e.g., a 2024 proximal modified quasi-Newton method and proximal trust-region methods with inexact evaluations), but no source clearly establishes a full proximal quasi-Newton convergence and complexity theory in Toint's general nonlinear stepsize control framework. Status is therefore not conclusively determined.

status_evidence.title: A Proximal Quasi-Newton Trust-Region Method for Nonsmooth Regularized Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Trust-region method for f+h with global convergence and O(1/ε^2) complexity; TR-R2 quadratic regularization variant.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the baseline trust-region convergence/complexity that the question asks to generalize to NSC.

status_evidence.title: A Proximal Modified Quasi-Newton Method for Nonsmooth Regularized Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up proximal modified quasi-Newton method for the same composite problem class.
status_evidence.claim: Related extensions exist, but not framed within general nonlinear stepsize control.

status_evidence.title: A proximal trust-region method for nonsmooth optimization with inexact function and gradient evaluations
status_evidence.snippet: Extension to inexact evaluations, not to general NSC framework.
status_evidence.claim: No verified extension to Toint's nonlinear stepsize control framework was found.
